slides.heading: Knapsack Problem
slides.subtitle: AlgoExpert · Hard · Dynamic Programming
slides.narration: Let's solve Knapsack Problem, a hard dynamic programming problem. We'll restate the problem, build the intuition, walk through the approach, read the Java solution, and finish with its complexity.

slides.heading: The problem
slides.narration: Here's the problem. Items are value, weight . Returns maxValue , item indices .

slides.heading: Intuition
bullets: Each item is taken or skipped; a table over items and capacities captures every choice.
slides.narration: Each item is taken or skipped; a table over items and capacities captures every choice.

slides.heading: Brute force vs optimal
bullets: 1-D array iterating capacity downward → O(C) space
slides.narration: Trying all subsets is exponential. A table over items and capacity is n times C, pseudo-polynomial, and backtracking recovers the items.

slides.heading: Approach
bullets: 1. Row per item, column per capacity
3. Take adds the value to the row above at capacity minus weight
slides.narration: Step by step. First, row per item, column per capacity. Second, skip copies the row above. Third, take adds the value to the row above at capacity minus weight. Fourth, backtrack to list items.

slides.caption: Item [1 value, 2 weight]
slides.narration: Add the item worth 1 weighing 2. Green cells improved by taking it. Best for capacity ten is now 1.

slides.caption: Answer: 10 using items [1, 3]
slides.narration: Backtracking from the bottom-right, the chosen items are [1, 3], worth 10.

slides.heading: Java solution
slides.narration: Dp of i, c is either skipping the item, or taking it if it fits. Then from the bottom-right, a change between rows means the item was taken.

slides.heading: Complexity
slides.narration: Time is O of n times c. Space is O of n times c.

slides.heading: Edge cases & pitfalls
slides.narration: This is pseudo-polynomial. The one-dimensional version must iterate capacity downward.

slides.heading: Recap
bullets: Each item is taken or skipped; a table over items and capacities captures every choice.
slides.narration: To recap Knapsack Problem: Each item is taken or skipped; a table over items and capacities captures every choice. Try re-implementing it from scratch without looking.
